item.text: {"results":[{"pair_id":"J02765","case1_error":"Adds costs for 14 individual balloons and two packs, purchasing 34 balloons instead of exactly 14.","case2_error":"Includes the stationary break in driving time when calculating distance.","reason":"The first combines redundant purchases; the second applies a driving speed to non-driving time.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J02766","case1_error":"Uses one bottle’s 80-load capacity as the total capacity of two bottles.","case2_error":"Evaluates the correctly written sum 9 + 9 + 9 + 8 + 8 + 8 as 49 instead of 51.","reason":"The first omits scaling capacity by bottle count; the second makes a numerical evaluation error.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J02767","case1_error":"Omits the stated 20% primer discount entirely.","case2_error":"Counts only five fruits when determining discount eligibility, although Mary buys ten.","reason":"Ignoring a discount entirely differs from applying its rule to an incorrectly restricted purchase count.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J02768","case1_error":"Treats the four overtime hours as occurring each day, multiplying their pay by five.","case2_error":"Multiplies the egg count directly by the price per dozen without converting eggs to dozens.","reason":"The first repeats overtime across days; the second mismatches quantity units and price units.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J02769","case1_error":"Gives an unsupported final value of 200 after correctly stating the formulas; those formulas yield 600.","case2_error":"Gives an unsupported final value of 450 after correctly stating the formulas; those formulas yield 75.","reason":"Both append incorrect final numbers to correct unevaluated formulas. Neither shows a calculation establishing a more specific error mechanism.","judgment":"same"}]}
